outcome: Give head of quality / clinical operations director a governed method to improve expired or unavailable study kits using site enrolment plans, depot stock and kit expiry dates, with final decisions…
overview: Clinical Supply Demand Forecasting addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in pharma and life sciences operations. The first proof of value uses site enrolment plans, depot stock and kit expiry dates. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is expired or unavailable study kits, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: site enrolment plans, depot stock and kit expiry dates; define expired or unavailable study kits and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Head of Quality / Clinical Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
